# ApkStart v0.5.8

This release addresses "whether it can actually run after installation, and what needs to be changed": it adds **system health check · auto-configuration**. After installation, click once to first find out whether CPU virtualization is enabled, whether the Windows Hypervisor Platform is available, the GPU and video memory, memory and system version; automatically change what can be automatically changed, provide buttons for things needing elevation, and explain clearly how to change things that can only be done in BIOS.

---

## 1. What is checked, and how

| Item | Method |
|---|---|
| CPU virtualization (VT-x / SVM) | `Win32_Processor` + BIOS-side flags |
| Whether Hyper-V / VBS is running | `Win32_ComputerSystem.HypervisorPresent` |
| Virtual Machine Platform (WHPX) | `Get-WindowsOptionalFeature`; when no permission, fall back to `WinHvPlatform.dll` + Hypervisor dual evidence |
| Whether hardware acceleration is currently available | `emulator -accel-check` (reuse cached conclusion) |
| AEHD driver | `System32\drivers\aehd.sys` |
| GPU / video memory / driver date | `Win32_VideoController` + registry `qwMemorySize` (`AdapterRAM` is truncated when >4GB, untrustworthy) |
| Memory / system version | `Win32_ComputerSystem` / `os.release()` |

**One pitfall that had to be written down**: after Hyper-V / memory integrity (VBS) takes over VT, `VMMonitorModeExtensions` and `SecondLevelAddressTranslationExtensions` return `False`. This machine is exactly that case (AMD 8745HS + WHPX available); the first version judged it as "CPU does not support virtualization" based on that, misreporting machines that can run hardware acceleration as unable to run. Now only when "no Hypervisor + acceleration also unavailable" is it judged unsupported; otherwise always marked unknown.

## 2. What is automatically configured

After clicking "Apply recommended configuration", it only writes these items (all safe, can be changed back at any time):

| Setting | Rule |
|---|---|
| Memory | 32GB→8GB / 16GB→6GB / 12GB→4GB / 8GB→3GB / smaller→2GB, and never more than half the host |
| CPU cores | 8 threads or more→4 cores; 4~7→2~3 cores; leave at least 1 core for Windows |
| Graphics quality | No acceleration or video memory <512MB→540×960, otherwise auto |
| Rendering backend | Acceleration available→leave to the automatic downgrade chain; no acceleration→`software` |
| Force software emulation | No acceleration→on |

At the same time, this machine's parameters are **solidified into a driver** (`auto-<vendor>-<build>.json`, priority 5), automatically applied on every boot from then on, without repeating the checkup. Drivers still must pass the 0.5.7 whitelist validation; content generated by the checkup cannot bypass parameter restrictions either.

## 3. What requires your participation

| Situation | UI |
|---|---|
| VT-x / SVM not enabled in BIOS | Only give steps (restart into BIOS → SVM Mode / Intel VT-x → Enabled); **do not pretend it can be one-clicked** |
| Windows feature not enabled (installer version) | "One-click enable (needs administrator)" → elevated enable HypervisorPlatform + VirtualMachinePlatform → prompt restart |
| Windows feature not enabled (Store version) | "Open the 'Windows Features' window" + checkbox instructions (MSIX is fixed at mediumIL, cannot elevate on its own) |
| No acceleration but CPU supports (installer version) | Additionally give "Install AEHD driver (needs administrator)" |
| GPU driver over 3 years old | Remind to go to the vendor's official site to update (do not automatically install drivers; installing the wrong version is worse) |

## 4. UI

The settings page adds "System health check · auto-configuration": conclusions listed one by one (green ok / yellow warn / red bad), each with a specific explanation and executable button; a one-sentence summary at the bottom + recommended configuration. The checkup takes about 2–3 seconds (one PowerShell gets all hardware info, another checks system features; auto-degrades when no permission).

## 5. Verification

- Added `test/preflight-test.js` **22 items**: resource recommendation boundaries, rendering backend suggestions, BIOS/Store/installer version three kinds of conclusions, WMI misjudgment regression, "auto-configuration only writes safe items", generated driver can pass driver validation, detection failure can still give a conclusion;
- Full plain Node test suite **309 items passing**;
- Hands-on on this machine: AMD 8745HS / Radeon 780M / 32GB / WHPX available → `level=good`, recommend 6GB + 4 cores + auto rendering, generate `auto-amd-26300` driver (swangle).

## Upgrade notes from 0.5.7

- `0.5.8.0 > 0.5.7.0`, Store can directly overwrite upgrade; installed apps, data, and snapshots are all retained.
- The checkup **does not run automatically**: it does nothing and changes nothing unless you tap "Start checkup".
- For users who previously manually set memory/cores: the checkup recommended values will overwrite these two items (that is the intent of "apply recommended configuration"); if you do not want to overwrite, do not tap apply, just view the report.
